title: Stream vs Sync Anchor Latency Comparison Dashboard
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Build a focused dashboard that compares tail and central latency (p50/p95/p99) across model routes with an explicit streaming-anchor view. This view should make it easy to identify where streaming I/O deviates from non-streaming (sync) response profiles for the same route and model version, and highlight cases where streaming introduces higher variance or tail risk.

Why: Many of our customers use both streaming responses (for lower apparent latency) and synchronous generation. Current dashboards separate streaming and sync metrics but lack an anchor comparison mode that ties both to the same request cohort, KV cache state, and model variant. This makes it hard to determine whether observed regressions in p99 are due to streaming logic, kernel selection, or upstream request-shaping.

Scope:
- New dashboard panel: "Stream-anchor comparator" which presents paired p50/p95/p99 times for streaming vs sync for the same model+route+time window.
- Cohort selection controls: sample by request size (tokens_in_prompt), session_kv_hit (true/false), and concurrency bucket.
- Trace hooks integration: add a lightweight trace link for all items above a configurable p95 threshold to surface the span waterfall.
- Time-windowed delta metric: compute p99_delta = p99_streaming - p99_sync and surface alerts when delta > 150ms for > 5m.
- Exportable CSV and link-to-trace for investigations.

Non-goals:
- Replacing existing route dashboards; this is a complementary comparator focused on paired analysis.
- Deep-rooted sampling changes to production tracing — we will rely on existing trace hooks and augment sampling for the delta-alert cohorts if approved.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dashboard shows paired p50/p95/p99 for streaming and sync for any selected model/route and time window.
- Cohort filters apply and update the paired metrics within 30s.
- Alerts fire when p99_delta exceeds configured threshold (default 150ms) and create links to the top 5 traces contributing to the delta.
- Instrumentation changes limited to adding annotated trace IDs on existing high-latency paths, no change to core serving runtime.

Implementation notes:
- Metrics source: use existing aggregated latency histograms in metrics pipeline (prometheus -> metrics-warehouse). We will compute percentiles using our histogram rollups and the new comparator query will join stream and sync histograms by route+model+time_bucket.
- Tracing: add optional span annotation 'serve.io.mode=streaming|sync' and ensure the trace hook capture includes kv_cache_hit boolean and kernel_variant tag. Coordinate with tracing team T-Trace to enable 1% sampling for delta-alert cohorts.
- UI: implement a paired-bar + delta-heatmap layout in console; reuse existing UX components for cohort controls and CSV export.
- Backend query performance: add pre-aggregated delta metric to metrics-warehouse to avoid expensive on-the-fly joins for large time windows.

Risk and mitigation:
- Risk: computing percentiles from large histograms might be slow for long windows. Mitigation: start with 1h/6h/24h pre-aggregates and roll forward.
- Risk: tracing sample increase could raise costs. Mitigation: keep sampling scoped to delta-alert cohorts and throttle to 1% by default.

- Prototype PR (frontend): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2248 (WIP)
- Backend aggregation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metrics-warehouse/pull/102 (draft)
